title: I didn't fully appreciate Operation Mincemeat until I saw It again
transcript: About 3 years ago, I went to see Operation Mincemeat for the first time and I absolutely loved the delivery of this show. The cast was amazing. This was the original cast who created the show, but I can't say that this has been my favorite musical like it is for some people cuz this is the best reviewed show in the history of the West End. It has received so many five stars and it has cult-like following. So, I decided to give it another go and now I have a slightly different perspective on it. And in this video, I'm going to share five things that you should know before you go see this show to make sure that you have the best time. If this is your first time on my channel, then welcome. I'm Christina. I go to theater every single week and here I share my theater reviews, tips, and also my creative journey. If you like the sound of it, then make sure to subscribe and like this video. You can also join my 2026 theater challenge by downloading the template in the description box below. The first and pretty unbelievable thing to know before you see Operation Mincemeat is that this is based partially on true events. This is an actual operation that happened within the Second World War where MI5 officers planted a corpse in the Spanish water so that these forged military documents end up in the hands of Hitler and trick him into thinking that allies are planning to invade Sardinia instead of Sicily. So, he moved his troops to Sardinia and then what happened is that the allies occupied Sicily and managed to save quite a lot of lives and advance in the winning of the war. But, the musical is a comedy and it is approaching this historical event with a lot of wittiness and self-deprecating British humor. So, witnessing this, you're actually witnessing part of history in the making but in a really funny interpretation which is written and initially delivered by SpitLip who are a musical comedy troupe that worked 6 years on this show before they started performing it in a smaller theater and then this show had its West End premiere in 2023 and now is actually also available on Broadway. So, this musical has gone a long way from a small fringe show, and today there are people who keep returning to it, to Fortune Theatre, or on Broadway, or even going from London to Broadway to actually see the new cast and experience this musical in so many different ways. So, there's a lot of heart and soul aside from all that humor and wit that comes with this musical that makes it just irresistible. So, the second thing to know before you see the musical is that despite the fact that this is a story about a war operation, it is delivered in such way that you are very much engaged with it, and you forget that there is a big gap between then and now. It is very contemporary and funny the way that the characters speak, and the way that they treat each other, and it feels that this war story is just the frame of the musical, whereas Spitlip has done an amazing job with painting the picture with so many different colors and ways and interpretations. And I think what the writers of the musical have done so well is that they leaned into the most absurd elements of British culture and humor to be able to really deliver this so it really resonates. So, there is a lot of laughter in the auditorium, and there are a lot of really witty sentences, and things that I feel are particular for the British culture, and they will help you resonate a bit better if you do have some understanding of the Brits and certain things such as institutions like MI5. Speaking of which, let's talk about the thing number three that I think you should know or be aware of before you go to see the musical, especially if English is not your first language. This is a very wordy musical. So, if you've experienced Hamilton or something like that, then you might be able to draw some parallel there because there is a lot of really fast-paced, maybe less rapping, but singing a lot of the time. It is full of very clever expressions, very witty remarks, and it is so fast-paced. So, you really need to be glued onto the characters to be able to follow. If you're just visiting London, I think this could be a harder musical to go and see as your first maybe musical experience or a musical that you don't know much about if English isn't your first language because it can get just tricky picking up on all those really fun elements of the show which actually make it so great. So in case that for example you still want to see Operation Mincemeat but English isn't your first language, then I would definitely recommend for you to familiarize yourself with the story line, with the characters, maybe even listen to the soundtrack a little bit on Spotify just so you kind of know roughly what the story is about. I think especially if you don't have context about the war or just generally how things have played out during that time, it would be a bit harder. The fourth thing to know before you go see Operation Mincemeat is that despite this musical being the witty, funny, and slightly absurd at times, it does carry a lot of emotional weight and that is the beauty of it and that is what kind of makes it not just a silly comedy. It makes it a comedy with really big and important final message of the show. The emotional anchor of the show is the song sung by Hester who is a secretary of the MI5 officers and this is the song called Dear Bill where Hester is writing this letter to basically explain to a younger secretary and younger MI5 agent how they should write a letter, a fake letter that was planted on the corpse. And she kind of goes on to say basically how you need to make people who are fighting the battle feel like they're just about to come back home and she kind of goes to talk about the roses in the garden and some mundane things to get to the point of how much she misses this person and it seems that throughout the song she's referring truly to someone that she has either lost in the war or someone that she's waiting to return. And this song is such a beautiful moment in the show, and it is one of those that just like make you feel the heaviness and also the brilliance of the show at the same time. It is definitely the number that has received the biggest ovation, and it is so unassuming and quiet to degree, but the words are so powerful, and they really dig into that feeling of what it feels like to wait for someone to come back from the war. There are a lot of these really beautiful moments trickled throughout the show. There is another shanty-type number that is called "Ceylon Boys". And in this song, there is a sentence where it says "To Ceylon boys, through stormy weather, soon the journey will be done." And just the way that this is delivered with these sailors who are carrying this corpse, and they're on that mission, it just felt really powerful. And it is really interesting how these moments are truly what stays with you after the show. Despite all the fun, exciting, comedic elements of the show, I feel like these are the songs that I kind of carry with me and that feeling that they made me feel. So, you definitely should be aware that this is not just a crazy hilarious comedy, but it has this beautiful emotional pull that makes it such a wonderful show to see. The fifth and the final thing to know is that the show is delivered only by five actors, but they are playing multiple characters, and this is what makes watching this show so brilliant. Cuz sometimes it's just takes a turn or a change of the prop to have a completely new character on stage. And just the way that they switch between them, the way that the blocking is done, that sometimes they move or change their costume behind the door on the stage, or they just take off the prop and they become this new person, it is so wonderful to see, and they are working really well together. So, I got to see the new cast for the next season in the West End, but I think it's a very much mirroring what the original cast has done, who was so close to the material, but I think that the legacy of it just continues to live because of the way that the show is written and the way that they cast these people who are just absolutely mind-blowingly talented. So, when you go to see the show, you can rest assured that you will see some of the best talent delivering some of the most spectacular performances, and it is also such a great show is that the men in the show are portrayed by women, and then Hester, the secretary, is performed by a man. So, there's a little bit of gender reversal when it comes to the roles. An interesting fact about all the characters in the Operation Mincemeat, the core characters, is that they are all based off of the real people who were involved in the Operation Mincemeat, and this is what makes this musical so incredible in the way that it's so thoroughly researched, and even Hester, who is the secretary and one of the emotional anchors of the show, she has her own plaque in the Fortune Theatre now because for years she hasn't been properly documented and her name has been like misspelled. So, actually the whole community surrounding this musical went on to find the name, and then in June 2023 they honored her with a plaque in the theater, which you can now see. It is safe to say that the second time seeing Operation Mincemeat for me definitely did the trick. I really love the show now, and again, it's not maybe one of my favorites that I'm going to go to regularly like I love Hadestown, but it's a brilliant show to see. It's one of the best in London and on Broadway, and it definitely deserves your attention. Have you seen Operation Mincemeat before? Let me know in the comments below, and if you need some more inspiration on what to see this year, then check out this video.
